batter_interpretation_risk.reading: asof_batter_* is the success rate of the PITCHES THROWN TO that batter, so a batter facing weak pitchers inherits their rate.  A large |corr| with the opposing-pitcher quality means the axis is a schedule proxy rather than a batter-skill signal; it does not by itself make the axis useless (schedule composition is legal, as-of information) but it changes what the column MEANS and is reported here rather than left implicit.

F4_not_run.gate_in_config: run only if F2 AND F3 both pass
F4_not_run.reason: F2 did not clear the pre-registered 3-sigma threshold, so the gate that would have launched F4 never opened.  This is reported as a gate outcome, not a silent omission.

stacker_curve_censoring.why: exp_046 A1 reported curve_argmin_is_interior=false on all three fold_2024 seeds, so its +45.17 was a lower bound.  exp_047 trains the stage-2 stacker past its policy iteration purely to LOCATE the argmin; iter_used is still the fold_2023-derived policy value, so fold_2024 selects nothing.
stacker_curve_censoring.policy_cost_is_a_cost_not_a_result: policy_cost_vs_extended_min_pts is how many points the arm gives up by honouring the iteration policy.  It is an ORACLE quantity (the minimum is located on fold_2024) and must never be reported as an achievable gain.

conclusions.one_line: All three arms rejected. The only axis that cleared the pre-registered stage-1 screen (ball, k=200) gave +6.89563 pts on fold_2024 (0.269x the 25.65339 threshold); the trajectory/deviation split disagreed in sign across seeds (+9.42414, 2/3). exp_046's success axis being special is the substantive finding.
conclusions.control: F1 (= exp_046 A1, 51 columns). The F1-R0 gap is exp_046's result and is NOT claimed here.
conclusions.selected_axis_and_why_only_one: Nine axes were diagnosed. All nine passed the incremental-R2 screen (residual >= 77.9%), so the existing 47 columns genuinely do not contain them. Six fell on block gain < 10 pts; `rev` fell on |r|=-0.81195 with the incumbent d_form_eb; `strk` fell on |r|=-0.73522 with `ball`. Only `ball` survived.
conclusions.🔴_design_flaw_found: The pre-registered filter had NO block-unit sign-agreement condition. `ball`'s block gain of +45.27429 is the average of [+116.85115, +110.95661, -22.53837, -24.17223] -- opposite signs across the 2022 and 2023 blocks. Its post-freeze fold_2024 offset read-out is -38.58266. A sign-agreement condition uses BLOCK-ONLY information (no fold_2024 contamination) and would have left only `rev` and `bsuc`. This rule was conceived AFTER seeing the values, so it is post-hoc and was NOT used to change any verdict here; it is proposed for the next pre-registration.
conclusions.F2R_is_exploratory_not_pre_registered: config's correlation rule says 'keep the larger-gain one', and `rev` (70.02150) out-gains the incumbent d_form_eb (53.83133). Since F2 is by construction a superset of F1, the incumbent cannot be dropped, so the implementation resolved the ambiguity by dropping the new axis -- code frozen before any value was read. F2R tests the opposite resolution and came out at -18.61904 (3/3 negative), so neither resolution would have produced an adoption. ⚠️ The decision to add F2R was taken after the fold_2024 offset read-out was visible, so it is post-hoc and is not used as adoption evidence.
conclusions.B_axis_barely_qualified: incremental block gain +10.17839 vs a 10-pt threshold (margin 0.18); corr(traj_eb, dev_eb) = -0.68366 vs a 0.7 ceiling (margin 0.016). config required traj and dev to be orthogonal for the design to hold; -0.684 is not orthogonal. F3's 2/3 sign split is consistent with that weakness.
conclusions.pitchmix_denominator_measured: asof_pitcher_pitchmix_n is elementwise EQUAL to asof_pitcher_n on 100.0% of rows, so the denominator question does not arise in this file. The three pitch-mix rates sum to exactly 1 on all 1,474,300 rows with n>0, so at most two of the three could enter; in practice all three fell on the gain threshold first and that filter never fired.
conclusions.batter_column_interpretation_risk: asof_batter_success_rate is the success rate of the pitches thrown TO that batter. Measured: batter-season deviation correlates +0.24465 with the weighted mean career success rate of the pitchers faced (1,225 batter-seasons), i.e. about 6% of its variance is opponent composition -- partly a schedule proxy, mostly not. bmid shows +0.04160, essentially none. Both axes fell on the gain threshold, so neither entered a model.
conclusions.iteration_policy_observation: Every arm and every seed had its fold_2024 stacker argmin at 1.2-2.6x the policy iteration (F1 550 vs 256; F2 475/675/525 vs 359; F2R 450/475/600 vs 231; F3 525/550/375 vs 308). The inherited rule `stage1 argmin x training-row ratio` is systematically short on fold_2024. This is a pipeline-level issue independent of the column sets and it applies identically to every arm here.
conclusions.LOO_requirement: config required F2's axes to be attributed by leave-one-out rather than by forward stepping. Exactly one axis passed, so LOO is automatic: removing `ball` IS F1, and F2 - F1 is that axis alone. No bundle was adopted from a forward-addition staircase.

not_run.F4: gate required BOTH F2 and F3 to pass; F2 did not. Gate outcome, not omission.
not_run.fold_2022: not run for any arm (exp_046 A1 did not run it either).
not_run.independent_leak_audit: NOT performed. New feature source + new time-series aggregation means this is audit-eligible under CLAUDE.md. No arm was adopted so nothing goes to a submission path, but the code must be audited before reuse.
not_run.inference_time: not measured -- no arm adopted, so no deployment path was built.

next_suggestions: Add a block-unit sign-agreement condition to the pre-registered axis screen.
Revisit the stage1->stage2 iteration inheritance rule (see iteration_policy_observation); it is a pipeline-level gain orthogonal to any column choice.

Ask why the success axis is special: nine axes plus the trajectory split all failed, which points at 'the column counts the same event as the target' rather than at a general 'decompose any diluted rate column' principle. rev's r=-0.81 with d_form_eb says the same thing (reverse is a failure mode of success).

⚠️ Do NOT record the nine axes as 'no signal'. What was measured is a 1-term linear offset probe for selection plus one column at a time in the tree. Non-linear combinations and interactions were not measured.

score_conversion_reminder: score digits beyond ~0.2 are a machine transform of a rounded Brier, not measured resolution (Brier 1e-6 = score 0.4003). Brier is the raw quantity; the score column is derived.
